newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber down limit on housing report.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber down limit on housing report.

text.p: A bearish U.S. housing starts report pushed January through May CME lumber futures down the daily $10.00 per thousand board foot limit near the opening, traders said.
January fell the limit to $384.80 per tbf and March the limit at $368.90 per tbf.

The Commerce Department reported October housing starts down 5.1 percent to 1.37 million annual rate, compared with the previous month. The figure represented the smallest number of starts in over a year. Permits were also down 2.7 percent and added to selling pressure, traders said.

Wall Street economists had an average forecast for October starts at 1.443 million unit annual rate. The building rate for single-family homes, the largest user of lumber, was the lowest since June 1995. Permits were at the lowest level since July 1995.

Lumber futures fell sharply to limit down Monday when the National Association of Home Builders reported its Housing Market Index at the slowest level since February. The news prompted concern over Tuesday's U.S. housing report and added to recent bearish sentiment on cash markets, traders added.
